brand.name: Pellory Ceramics
brand.positioning: Wheel-thrown stoneware for the kitchen shelf, made by the river in Quarry Bend.
brand.origin: Before June Avery threw her first pot in a rented garage, she surveyed land for a living. She still keeps her old field notebook beside the wheel.
brand.profile_bio: Stoneware mugs, bowls and planters. Online & at Saturday market. Six wheels on Thursday nights.

headline: Thirty days of Instagram
for a one-woman pottery studio.
intro.deck: June, I'd start with the story only you can tell: how a surveyor ended up at a wheel in a rented garage. Over the next month, we'll use it to fill Thursday wheel classes, open the December kiln drop and build your newsletter list.
intro.calendar_note: Day 1 starts on Monday. A Story goes up every day, including feed days. Friday, Day 26 is the December kiln-opening drop. The pillar shares guide the feed mix, rounded to a whole post.

captions.first_line: A map taught me to throw pots.
captions.body:
A map taught me to throw pots.

Before I had a wheel, I carried a field book through wet grass. In my rented garage I used the same book to write down how far a rim dropped when I pulled too hard.

Now the book sits beside the splash pan. It smells faintly of clay, and half the pencil marks have a thumbprint through them.

Join the studio newsletter through the link in bio for the next page from my field book.
captions.alt_text: Pencil contour lines curve across June's field notebook beside a blue stoneware mug. Cover text reads From field notes to clay.

captions.body:
Watch the wobble go quiet.

Wet clay keeps tapping your palm until it's centered. I can usually hear the wheel settle at about the same moment I feel that tap stop.

The thing I tell beginners is to brace their elbows before they add pressure. That tiny change makes the wheel feel a lot less bossy.

Save this for the next time your clay won't sit still.
captions.alt_text: An overhead view shows a mound of clay centered on the wheel head. Cover text reads Find the middle.

captions.body:
What if it wobbles?

The first sound you'll hear is the splash pan rattling a bit as the wheel gets going. The clay might lean. Mine leaned for weeks.

Thursday nights have six seats. I'll show you how to brace your hands and help you get your clay back to the middle when it wanders.

Book a Thursday wheel class through the link in bio.
captions.alt_text: A white towel rests by the wheel and a small wet bowl sits on a board. Cover text reads Your first Thursday.

captions.first_line: This mug is upside down for a reason.
captions.body:
This mug is upside down for a reason.

The best noise in the garage is the one a leather-hard cup makes when a loop tool catches just enough clay. It comes off in a ribbon, the way cold butter curls.

I trim a shallow foot so a mug has a clean place to meet the table. It's the part you'll see when you tip up the last sip.

Save this if you want to look for the foot on your own cup.
captions.alt_text: An upside-down clay mug sits on a wheel head with a ribbon of trimming beside it. Cover text reads Under the cup.

captions.body:
Three grips. Same mug.

When I pull a handle, I try it with damp hands. That's how I find the spot where a thumb actually wants to rest.

This Ferry Blue mug has a wide bend above the join. I leave a little extra room there for a second finger.

Tell me which grip you'd use on a cold morning.
captions.alt_text: A blue mug is seen from the side, with the handle clear against a folded oatmeal-colored towel. Cover text reads Three ways to hold it.

captions.first_line: POV: the kiln is finally cool.
captions.body:
POV: the kiln is finally cool.

The kiln's cool enough to open, and the flat gray on the test tile has turned into the color of the banks after rain. The Ferry Blue is darkest where the handles join. That's the line I look for first.

I've set the mugs, bowls and planters by the window to check the rims and feet one more time.

Shop the December kiln-opening batch through the link in bio.
captions.alt_text: The open kiln reveals shelves of stoneware, including Ferry Blue mugs and a shallow rust-colored bowl. Cover text reads December kiln opening.

captions.first_line: Ferry Blue came from the shadow under a ferry.
captions.body:
Ferry Blue came from the shadow under a ferry.

I take the glaze tiles to my window before I name them. Slate Run looks like wet stone. Rust Bank looks like the line you can see on the steps after the river goes down. Oat Milk has the little specks I kept losing under the bench light.

Save this color guide for the December kiln opening.
captions.alt_text: Six illustrated slides show river contours and four glazes: gray Slate Run, Ferry Blue, brick Rust Bank and speckled cream Oat Milk. The last slide gives the Day 26 drop date.

captions.first_line: Your first bowl can lean a little.
captions.body:
Your first bowl can lean a little.

Wear something that'll wash. There's a towel by each wheel. I'll show you where to put your elbows and how to open the clay with your thumb.

When we're done, the bowl stays with me to dry. I'll explain firing and pickup before you head back out to the river road.

Book one of the six Thursday seats through the link in bio.
captions.alt_text: Six illustrated slides show a first Thursday wheel class, from clothes and centering through drying and pickup, ending with instructions to book.

captions.first_line: Here's what made it to the window shelf.
captions.body:
Here's what made it to the window shelf.

I line up the finished pots in the window before I pack them. That's where I spotted the darker blue at the mug handles and the thin red line where the glaze breaks on the planters.

There's a shallow Slate Run bowl in the batch that feels especially good in both hands.

See the December kiln-opening collection through the shop link in bio.
captions.alt_text: Five illustrated slides show the kiln, a Ferry Blue mug, a Slate Run bowl and a Rust Bank planter, followed by a shop direction.

goals.source: Log post insights after an equal reporting window. Divide saves and shares separately by reach where reach is available.

review: Log each post's goal, pillar, format and link tag so it can be compared with posts doing the same job.
Check that bio links and Story stickers still land on the intended pages before the next scheduled post.
Reconcile booking, shop and email exports. Mark missing attribution as unknown.
Read replies for recurring questions. Turn one into next week's Story and note why it made the list.

tests.name: Reel opening line
tests.hypothesis: A sensory instruction keeps people watching longer than a direct question.
tests.how: Cut two versions of Find the middle with the same footage, runtime, cover and caption. Change only the opening line: ‘Watch the wobble go quiet’ vs ‘Can you spot the wobble?’ Run them in matched posting slots away from launch week.
tests.compare: Compare the share of viewers still watching at the same early point, with the same time since publication.
tests.decision: Test thresholds: at least 200 plays per version and a 5 percentage point lead. If either threshold is missed, keep the original and repeat. Treat the comparison as directional.

tests.name: Carousel cover wording
tests.hypothesis: A beginner question earns more saves per reach than a class description.
tests.how: Use the same first-class deck with a question cover and a statement cover in matched slots. Hold the layout, caption and booking direction steady.
tests.compare: Compare saves per reach at the same post age. Use booking taps as context.
tests.decision: Test thresholds: at least 200 reached per version and a 20% relative lift in saves per reach. If either threshold is missed or the baseline is zero, repeat.

tests.name: Lunch vs evening Stories
tests.hypothesis: Evening is an easier time for locals to tap a class booking link.
tests.how: Show the same booking Story at lunch and in the early evening on comparable days. Alternate which time goes first across matched weeks, outside the drop.
tests.compare: Compare sticker taps per frame reach for each time after the Story expires.
tests.decision: Test thresholds: at least 100 reached per time slot in total and a 15% relative lift. If either threshold is missed or the baseline is zero, keep both slots in rotation and repeat.
